title: Decisions, with evidence
authorship: TasteForge agent-authored annotations of preserved, agent-authored UI captures

cases.title: Give the stock columns distinct meanings
cases.purpose: Work: compare stock quantities without guessing which column they belong to.
cases.evidence: The 320px entry produced a 327px-wide document. Available and Shortage visually collided in the actual capture.
cases.change: Reserve room for numeric headings and use a readable mixed-case treatment at narrow widths.
cases.keep: Keep the comparable stock table and explicit units. A table is appropriate for this task.
cases.limit: This repairs the named 320px state; it does not establish readability under every font, zoom level or language.

captures.label: Before · crowded headings
captures.alt: Inventory table with Available and Shortage headings crowded together at a 320px viewport.
captures.note: The two headings run together. The image is 327px wide because the page overflows its 320px viewport.

captures.label: After · distinguishable headings
captures.alt: Revised inventory table with separate Available and Shortage labels aligned above their values.
captures.note: Each quantity has its own visible column label. Recorded document width now matches the 320px viewport.

cases.title: Expose the focused recovery action
cases.purpose: Work: recover from a failed local decision without losing the item or quantity.
cases.evidence: Retry was focused but its document bounds were y744–788 while the 740px-high viewport remained at scrollY 0.
cases.change: Allow focus to expose Retry, then check its actual viewport bounds after inserting the failure state.
cases.keep: Retain the stock evidence, requested quantity, explicit failure text and coloured error rule. Scrolling is acceptable when it exposes recovery with the necessary context.
cases.limit: The before image is full-page with a viewport boundary; the after image is an actual viewport capture after scrolling. Their different framing is intentional and labelled.

captures.label: Before · focus below the viewport
captures.alt: Full-page failed-decision capture; Retry is just below the marked 740px viewport boundary.
captures.note: The full image includes Retry, but it was not exposed in the original viewport. Being in a full-page screenshot is not evidence of visibility.

captures.label: After · recovery exposed by focus
captures.alt: Actual 320 by 740 viewport after scrolling: item, quantity, failure message, Retry and Edit remain visible.
captures.note: At scrollY 136, Retry is around y608–652 within the actual viewport. Identity, consequence, failure and Edit remain visible too.

cases.title: Say where Back will take the operator
cases.purpose: Work: inspect one item and return to the same filtered stock search.
cases.evidence: The earlier label said Back to stock. The implementation retained search/filter state, but the label did not communicate that context.
cases.change: Use Back to filtered stock when search or filtering is active. Retention behaviour stays intact.
cases.keep: Keep a single compact return control. There is no need to repeat the complete list or every filter value above the decision.
cases.limit: This is a local clarity improvement supported by screenshots and the supplied return trace, not measured comprehension or speed.

captures.label: Before · generic destination
captures.alt: Mobile decision review with a Back to stock control.
captures.note: The plain destination gives little cue that the current search and shortage filter will be restored.

captures.label: After · retained context is explicit
captures.alt: Mobile decision review with a Back to filtered stock control.
captures.note: The label now names the retained result context. The return trace separately checks the actual query, filter and focus.

cases.title: Choose the overview/detail relationship
cases.purpose: Work: decide on one stock item while retaining a way back to comparison.
cases.evidence: Both neutral candidates use the same fixture and behaviour and complete the scripted review/edit/failure/retry path.
cases.change: The selected main example focuses detail on mobile while retaining side-by-side comparison on desktop.
cases.keep: A continuous overview can be appropriate when repeated cross-item comparison dominates. This choice trades simultaneous mobile comparison for a dedicated task view.
cases.limit: These are structural alternatives, not chronological before/after versions, a randomized A/B test or a measured user preference.

captures.label: A · continuous overview
captures.alt: Neutral continuous mobile prototype with five stock rows above the selected item's review.
captures.note: The full overview remains above the decision. Record is around document y1360; the initial viewport is 844px high.

captures.label: B · focused detail
captures.alt: Neutral focused mobile prototype with identity, stock evidence, quantity, consequence and actions together.
captures.note: The review is the active view; Back retains list context. Record is around y621. Position alone does not establish ease of use.
